corrected_proposal.title: Trump Pardoned William E. Henry on January 19, 2021
corrected_proposal.description_short: Trump pardoned William E. Henry on January 19, 2021, for a federal theft-of-government-property conviction.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: The Justice Department lists William E. Henry under January 19, 2021 pardons, with the Middle District of Alabama, theft of government property, and a sentence of two years’ probation plus a $4,000 fine dated May 2, 2019. The listing does not state Trump’s reason for granting clemency.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On January 19, 2021, Donald Trump granted a pardon to William E. Henry, whom the Department of Justice Office of the Pardon Attorney lists under that date. The official table names Henry, identifies the Middle District of Alabama, and lists theft of government property as the offense. It records two years’ probation and a $4,000 fine, with the sentence dated May 2, 2019. Those entries document the person, federal district, offense label, and sentence associated with the clemency grant. The table does not explain why Trump selected Henry, describe the conduct behind the conviction, or report an exchange or other private benefit. The fact of a pardon alone does not establish a corrupt motive. Accordingly, this entry describes a documented presidential pardon while leaving motive and underlying case facts unknown. No exchange, financial loss, political favoritism, or public reaction is documented in the DOJ table.
